source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Apply firm direct pressure to the affected eye, which is not the appropriate immediate action for this kind of chemical eye injury","B":"Instill antibiotic ointment immediately without irrigation, similar to what the coworker is currently reaching for before anything else","C":"Begin immediate, copious irrigation for an extended period, rather than reaching for ointment first as the coworker is currently suggesting","D":"Apply a dry dressing and wait for provider evaluation, which delays the truly urgent irrigation this kind of injury actually requires"}}
source_row.rationale: The priority action for a chemical splash injury to the eye is immediate, copious irrigation with water or normal saline, continuing for an extended period (often 15-20 minutes or longer, depending on the specific chemical and clinical guidance), to dilute and remove the chemical as quickly as possible and minimize ongoing tissue damage, before further evaluation and treatment.
source_row.source_detail: Priority of Immediate, Copious Eye Irrigation
source_row.source_name: American Academy of Ophthalmology — Chemical Eye Injury Emergency Management
